statement: Let P be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] > 0. Let Z be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] = 0. Let S be the sum of nums[i] over all i with nums[i] > 0. Let b be the list obtained by taking all values -nums[i] for indices with nums[i] < 0, then sorting them in nondecreasing order; write m = len(b). Let k be the largest integer with 0 <= k <= m such that either k = 0 or the sum over t = 0 to k-1 of b[t] is strictly less than S, where the sum is the empty sum 0 when k=0. Then max_score(nums) returns a result r and r = P + k + (if S > 0 then Z else 0).
preconditions: nums is a nonempty slice of 64-bit integers, 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: For every input satisfying the constraints, max_score(nums) returns a result r; it does not fail (no panic, out-of-bounds access, or arithmetic overflow).
preconditions: nums is a nonempty slice of 64-bit integers, 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever max_score(nums) returns a result r, we have 0 <= r <= len(nums).
preconditions: nums is a nonempty slice of 64-bit integers, 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Let P be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] > 0. Whenever max_score(nums) returns a result r, we have r >= P.
preconditions: nums is a nonempty slice of 64-bit integers, 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Let P be the number of indices i with nums[i] > 0, let Z be the number of indices i with nums[i] = 0, and let S be the sum of all positive entries nums[i]. If S > 0, then whenever max_score(nums) returns a result r, we have r >= P + Z.
preconditions: nums is a nonempty slice of 64-bit integers, 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: If nums[0] > 0, then max_score(nums) returns 1; if nums[0] <= 0, then max_score(nums) returns 0.
preconditions: nums is a nonempty slice of 64-bit integers satisfying the constraints, and len(nums) = 1.

statement: max_score(nums) returns a result r and r = 0.
preconditions: nums is a nonempty slice of 64-bit integers satisfying the constraints, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), nums[i] <= 0.

statement: Let T be the sum of all entries nums[i] for 0 <= i < len(nums). Then max_score(nums) returns a result r, and r = len(nums) if and only if T > 0.
preconditions: nums is a nonempty slice of 64-bit integers, 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Let n = len(nums) and let r be the result of max_score(nums). There exists a bijection p from {0,1,...,n-1} to {0,1,...,n-1} such that the number of indices i with 0 <= i < n and the sum over j = 0 to i of nums[p(j)] > 0 is exactly r.
preconditions: nums is a nonempty slice of 64-bit integers, 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Let n = len(nums) and let r be the result of max_score(nums). For every bijection p from {0,1,...,n-1} to {0,1,...,n-1}, the number of indices i with 0 <= i < n and the sum over j = 0 to i of nums[p(j)] > 0 is at most r.
preconditions: nums is a nonempty slice of 64-bit integers, 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever max_score(nums) returns r and max_score(nums2) returns r2, we have r = r2.
preconditions: nums and nums2 are nonempty slices of 64-bit integers satisfying the constraints, and nums2 is a permutation of nums: len(nums2) = len(nums) and there is a bijection p from {0,1,...,len(nums)-1} to {0,1,...,len(nums)-1} with nums2[i] = nums[p(i)] for all i.

statement: Let P be the number of positive entries of nums, Z the number of zero entries, S the sum of positive entries, and b the nondecreasing list of the absolute values of the negative entries of nums. Let k be the largest integer with 0 <= k <= len(b) such that either k = 0 or the sum of the first k entries of b is strictly less than S, with the empty sum equal to 0. Then whenever max_score(nums) returns a result r, r - P - (if S > 0 then Z else 0) = k.
preconditions: nums is a nonempty slice of 64-bit integers, 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Let r be the result returned by max_score(nums) and r2 the result returned by max_score(nums2). Then r2 >= r + 1.
preconditions: nums and nums2 are nonempty slices of 64-bit integers satisfying the constraints. nums2 has length len(nums)+1, its multiset of entries is the multiset of nums together with one additional integer c, and c > 0.

statement: Let T be the sum of all entries of nums. If T <= 0, then whenever max_score(nums) returns r, r <= len(nums) - 1.
preconditions: nums is a nonempty slice of 64-bit integers, 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Let a be the list obtained by sorting the entries of nums in nonincreasing order, and let pref[i] = sum_{j=0}^i a[j] for 0 <= i < len(nums). Then max_score(nums) returns a result r, and r is the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and pref[i] > 0.
preconditions: nums is a nonempty slice of 64-bit integers, 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.
